newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end weaker but off lows.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end weaker but off lows.

text.p: SPI futures 2388 -8 US 30yr cl 6.45 +0.03
10yrbond futs 92.865 -0.025 Gold (NY cl) 375.05 +.65
*Stocks end weaker but buying returns in afternoon to lift market off midsession lows. Volume 410.53 million shares, value A$807.24 million, 1084 stocks traded, 328 steady, 379 up, 277 down.
Australian shares closed weaker on Wednesday but were lifted off the midsession lows by bargain hunting in the afternoon session.
At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was down 5.3 points at 2,376.7.
December share price index futures were eight points lower at 2,388 and were at an 11.3 point premium to the index.
The leaders saw a choppy day's trading with little real trend apparent. Most swung to and fro around square, but all closed off their lows as traders spotted value around the day's lows.
"You started to see some buying come back into it," said a Sydney-based dealer.
Activity was mixed with the day generally one of small losses or small gains and with the single figure end result widely expected.
"Banks were stronger and the gold index was slightly better. Most losses were in the transport, media and insurance," the dealer said.
Best performers among the leaders were major miners CRA and WMC, which both ended firmer, 23 cents and nine cents respectively above their intraday lows.
Outside the leaders, though, the pace was frenetic in the small miners, particularly those prospecting in the Gawler Craton region in South Australia.

Helix Resources shares doubled in value to A$3.70 from A$1.85 after a drilling report early in the day that confirmed additional significant gold mineralisation at its Lake Everard Project in the Gawler Craton region.
Other miners with exploration interests in the area also rocketed as players punted on the region as a gold play.
Rises just shaded falls, while 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivatives trading was active, the choppy day's performance ensuring positions had to be covered.
Total options traded 61,940 (54,594)
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 7,995 (9,644)

In other local markets, Australian bond yields closed higher after being whipped around in active trading with technical weakness in futures proving the overriding factor, despite Japan's quarterly Tankan report showing continued weakness and ensuring further flows from Japanese investors into Australia.
By 5.25 p.m. (0625 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.115 percent.

The Australian dollar put in another steady performance against its U.S. counterpart as a generally upbeat market waited for recent gains to be fully absorbed before testing major resistance at US$0.8150.

Traders said bulls were frustrated by options-related sales close to US$0.8130, but had so far found good support around US$0.8075 which convinced most dealers that any further dip should be regarded as a buying opportunity.
By 5.25 p.m. the local currency was quoted at US$0.8089/94.
